chapter.name: Making of the Constitution
chapter.blurb: The demand for a Constituent Assembly, its composition and working, committees, enactment, enforcement and criticism.

concepts.name: Demand for a Constituent Assembly
concepts.description: How the idea of a Constituent Assembly grew from 1934 to the Cabinet Mission.
concepts.idea: The demand for an Assembly to frame India's Constitution moved from an idea in 1934 to a British acceptance in 1940 and a Cabinet Mission plan in 1946.
concepts.rule: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India in 1934. In 1935 the Indian National Congress officially demanded one, and in 1938 Jawaharlal Nehru declared that the Constitution of free India must be framed without outside interference by an Assembly elected on adult franchise; the Congress reiterated this in 1939. The British Government accepted the demand in principle in the August Offer of 1940. Sir Stafford Cripps brought a draft proposal in 1942, but the Muslim League rejected it because it wanted two separate Constituent Assemblies. A Cabinet Mission was then sent; it rejected two assemblies but gave a scheme that more or less satisfied the League.
concepts.example: The Cabinet Mission of 1946 had three members and published its plan on 16 May 1946.

concepts.name: Composition of the Constituent Assembly
concepts.description: The scheme of the Cabinet Mission: 389 seats, election and election results.
concepts.idea: The Assembly of 1946 was partly elected, partly nominated, and indirectly chosen.
concepts.rule: The Constituent Assembly was formed in November 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. Its planned strength was 389: 296 for British India and 93 for the princely states. Of the 296, 292 came from eleven governors' provinces and four from the four Chief Commissioners' provinces. Seats went roughly one for every million people. Seats of each province were divided among Muslims, Sikhs and General communities, and representatives were elected by members of their community in the provincial assembly by proportional representation with the single transferable vote. Princely-state members were nominated by their rulers. In the July-August 1946 elections the Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and others the remaining 15; the 93 princely-state seats were not filled at first. Gandhi was the important personality missing. The Assembly was not directly elected on adult franchise, but it represented all sections of society including women.
concepts.example: The Constituent Assembly had 15 women members, such as Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta.

concepts.name: Working of the Assembly and the Objectives Resolution
concepts.description: The first meeting, the office-bearers and the Objectives Resolution of 1946.
concepts.idea: The Assembly began work on 9 December 1946, and Nehru's Objectives Resolution set out its philosophy.
concepts.rule: The Assembly met first on 9 December 1946. The Muslim League boycotted it and only 207 members attended. Dr Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member, was temporary Chairman. On 11 December Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent Chairman. H.C. Mukherjee became Vice-President on 25 January 1947 and T. Krishnamachari the second Vice-President in July 1947. On 13 December 1946 Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution, which declared India an independent sovereign republic and promised a Union of territories, autonomous units with residuary powers, power derived from the people, justice, equality and freedom, and safeguards for minorities and backward classes. It was adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947 and its modified form became the Preamble.
concepts.example: The Assembly adopted the Objectives Resolution on 22 January 1947.

concepts.name: Changes by the Independence Act and other functions of the Assembly
concepts.description: How partition and the 1947 Act changed the Assembly, and what else it did besides framing the Constitution.
concepts.idea: After the Independence Act the Assembly became sovereign and also the Dominion Legislature.
concepts.rule: After the Mountbatten Plan of 3 June 1947 most princely states joined the Assembly. The Indian Independence Act of 1947 made the Assembly fully sovereign, able to frame any Constitution and to alter or repeal British laws for India. It also became a legislative body, so it made the Constitution and ordinary laws on separate days: as the Constituent body it was chaired by Dr Rajendra Prasad and as legislature by G.V. Mavalankar. After the Muslim League members from areas of Pakistan withdrew, its strength fell from 389 to 299: 229 for the provinces and 70 for the princely states. The Assembly also ratified India's Commonwealth membership in May 1949, adopted the national flag on 22 July 1947, and the national anthem and national song on 24 January 1950, and elected Rajendra Prasad as the first President on 24 January 1950. It held 11 sessions over 2 years 11 months 18 days, studied constitutions of about 60 countries, considered the draft for 114 days and spent Rs 64 lakh. It then served as the provisional Parliament until the first general elections of 1951-52.
concepts.example: The Assembly met as the Dominion Legislature first on 17 November 1947 and elected Mavalankar Speaker.

concepts.name: Committees of the Constituent Assembly and the Drafting Committee
concepts.description: Major and minor committees, their chairs, and the seven-member Drafting Committee.
concepts.idea: The Assembly worked through eight major committees, with the Drafting Committee the most important.
concepts.rule: The Assembly appointed eight major committees and several minor ones. Union Powers and Union Constitution Committees and the States Committee were chaired by Nehru; the Provincial Constitution Committee by Sardar Patel; the Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal Areas by Patel, with J.B. Kripalani heading the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee and H.C. Mukherjee the Minorities Sub-Committee; the Rules of Procedure and Steering Committees by Rajendra Prasad; and the Drafting Committee by Dr B.R. Ambedkar. Among the minor ones, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar headed the Credentials Committee, Pattabhi Sitaramayya the House Committee and K.M. Munshi the Order of Business Committee. The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 with seven members: Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (who replaced B.L. Mitter) and T.T. Krishnamachari (who replaced D.P. Khaitan). It published the first draft in February 1948, allowed eight months for public comment, and published a second draft in October 1948.
concepts.example: The Drafting Committee sat for only 141 days.

concepts.name: Enactment, enforcement and criticism of the Constitution
concepts.description: The three readings, adoption on 26 November 1949, commencement on 26 January 1950, the Hindi text, key persons and criticisms.
concepts.idea: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950.
concepts.rule: Ambedkar introduced the final draft on 4 November 1948; five days of general discussion followed. The second reading ran from 15 November 1948 to 17 October 1949, with 7,653 amendments proposed and 2,473 discussed. The third reading began on 14 November 1949 and the Constitution was passed on 26 November 1949, signed by 284 of 299 members. It then had a Preamble, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules. Ambedkar is called the Father of the Constitution. Constitution Day is celebrated on 26 November since 2015. Some provisions (citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament, and others such as Articles 5 to 9, 60, 324, 366, 367, 379, 380, 388, 391, 392 and 393) came into force at once, and the rest on 26 January 1950, chosen because of Purna Swaraj Day of 1930. The 1935 and 1947 Acts were repealed. The elephant was the seal of the Assembly; B.N. Rau was constitutional adviser, H.V.R. Iyengar the Secretary, S.N. Mukherjee chief draftsman and Prem Behari Narain Raizada the calligrapher, with decoration by Nand Lal Bose and Beohar Rammanohar Sinha. The 58th Amendment (1987) inserted Article 394A on the Hindi text. Critics said the Assembly was not representative or sovereign, was slow, Congress-dominated, lawyer-dominated and Hindu-dominated; Naziruddin Ahmed called the Drafting Committee a 'Drifting Committee'.
concepts.example: Republic Day is celebrated on 26 January because Purna Swaraj Day was observed on that date in 1930.
